add.title: LGBTQ people in prison — Canada section (Wikipedia)
add.summary: Placement policy: after Bill C-16 (2017) banned discrimination based on gender identity, transgender prisoners were to be placed in correctional facilities based on their gender identity, and Prime Minister Trudeau promised to review transgender prison assignment to ensure facilities match gender identity; transgender prisoners imprisoned for more than 12 continuous months are to be considered for sex-reassignment surgery. A 2022 study of Nova Scotia correctional officers found them generally mindful of trans-prisoner safety and security but with some concerns about risk to other prisoners; a 2022 CTV report alleged gender-diverse prisoners face a pattern of abuse and discrimination in Canadian jails and are more likely to be victims of sexual assault. No special-unit or solitary/segregation policy detail beyond the federal identity-based placement rule.

add.title: Barbara findlay (Wikipedia) — Synthia Kavanagh case
add.summary: Documented case: the article records that Canadian lawyer Barbara findlay represented Synthia Kavanagh, a transgender prisoner, in litigation concerning gender-affirming medical treatment and placement in a women's correctional institution — evidence that Canadian trans-prisoner placement and gender-affirming care were litigated in court. The Wikipedia article gives no dates or final outcome for the case, so this add is thin on specifics.
